author: Mark Atwood
text:
Fixed via the bead's minimal-fix path (doc additions). Added a sub-section under the 'realistic-demo-ids enabled' branch of demo_next_id rustdoc covering:
  1. The fallback value 1_000_000_000 and the clock-before-1970 trigger condition (with a recognizable id signature 0x...3b9aca01 for diagnostic purposes).
  2. SystemTime non-monotonicity (NTP adjustments, cross-restart clock skew) per the std::time docs, scoped to a realistic explanation of when it actually bites a demo binary.
  3. wrapping_add cycle behavior (584-year theoretical concern; flagged as cosmetic only).

Did NOT apply the bead's optional 'use Instant::now().elapsed() relative to a process-start OnceLock<Instant>' refactor — Instant is not monotonic across processes either (Instant::now is monotonic only within one process), so swapping SystemTime for Instant trades one non-monotonicity flavor for another without genuine improvement. The bead labeled this 'optionally' / option (3); not pursuing it is consistent with the bead's verdict.

The demo nature of demo_next_id remains dominant; this is teach-by-example cleanup, not production-grade hardening. Verified: cargo fmt clean, RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc clean (both with and without --all-features), cargo test --all-features 120+13+1 passed.
